newsitem.title: UK: Nickel closes LME at new lows, others mixed.
newsitem.headline: Nickel closes LME at new lows, others mixed.

text.p: Nickel prices fell to fresh 2-1/4 year lows during late Monday LME trading, as negative sentiment increased with further losses expected, traders said.
Elsewhere in the metals complex business was generally slow as is usual in the dead period between the Christmas and New Year holidays, and prices were mixed.

This pattern is likely to continue throughout the rest of this week, although there will be spells of interest from Tuesday's warehouse stock data, and January traded options, which will be declared on Thursday - the first business day of 1997. Nickel fell sharply again today, continuing last week's trend, with prices pressured by further liquidation and speculative sales. Some support was attempted around $6,400 before a late sell-off dumped the market down to its low of $6,365, down $111 from Friday.
Warehouse stocks are seen in an uptrend, while the clear breach of $6,400 suggests that the next chart support level of $6,330 will now be tested, they said.
Copper trading was inconclusive throughout the session, with few clear trends seen in either outright prices or the spreads. A late kerb flip-up ensured a steadier close at $2,129, up $2.
Aluminium held in a narrow range and was capably supported above the $1,540 level, against a background of physical interest for first quarter 1997.
Prices also perked up in late business, finishing the kerb at $1,550, up $4 from the previous close.

Lead dropped under $700 at one stage, but encountered some support with traders citing current cold weather in Europe which will assist replacement battery demand. However, last business was at $703, still down $10.
Zinc also looks vulnerable after sliding back under $1,070, with a test of $1,060 expected if business remains slow. Last kerb business was at $1,068, down $7.
Tin and aluminium alloy traded quietly, and both ended at steady levels of $5,740 and $1,392/95 respectively.
